subject: SLA anchor & right-size GPU pool for high-throughput chat workload
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@apexmed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@apexmed.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing + SLA ask for chat product

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re in procurement & infra sync this week and need a concrete proposal for dedicated capacity so we can move this to our procurement queue. High level workload profile attached (apex_workload_summary.csv). Key numbers: 

- Peak request profile: 350 requests/second sustained during business hours, with short spikes to ~600 r/s (3–5 min)
- Average tokens per request (incl. prompt + response): ~200 tokens
- Typical context length: 4k tokens (long chat history retained for some flows)
- Concurrency: baseline ~40, spikes ~80
- Model mix: primarily optimized 13B-like open model most traffic, about 10% of requests require a 70B-class model for clinical reasoning flows
- Latency targets: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 700ms for the 13B path (we can tolerate slower for the 70B path)

Questions for your proposal: recommended reserved GPU pool (type & count), burst/auto-scale strategy, baseline guaranteed throughput and how you’d reflect that in a monthly commit, and a ballpark committed spend and discount for a 12-month term. Also please attach any SOC2 / security artifacts or links for procurement.

Can you get a proposal by EOD Wednesday (11/11)? Our procurement owner copied.

—Sarah
Sarah Li
Head of Platform 
ApexMed

--- Attachment: apex_workload_summary.csv (CSV, 34KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@apexmed.com>, procurement@apexmed.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing + SLA ask for chat product

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear profile and the attachment; that helps a lot. High-level response below and we’ll follow up with a one-page MAP and pricing table tomorrow. Quick answers up front: we can commit to a throughput-backed SLA and a 12-month reserved GPU proposal that gives you headroom for sustained 350 r/s and short spikes.

Sizing reasoning (short):
- 200 tokens/request @ 350 r/s = ~70k tokens/s sustained. With microbatching and prefix KV caching for session-state we estimate token throughput per GPU materially increases.
- For your model mix we recommend a two-tier pool: primary pool for the 13B-weighted traffic and a smaller pool (or shared burst capacity) for the 70B flows.

Recommendation (initial):
- Reserved: 6 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs dedicated to the 13B path (covers sustained 350 r/s with ~20% headroom using our batching and KV caching).
- Burst/Autoscale: +4 GPUs in a burst pool (automatically available for spikes up to ~600 r/s for 3–5 min windows).
- 70B workload: 2 x A100-80GB-equivalents (or 4x A10G depending on perf/cost trade) in a smaller reserved pool that can be shared for critical flows; we’ll price both options.

SLA / Guarantees:
- Throughput guarantee: 350 r/s sustained for the 13B path (monthly uptime/throughput SLA; exceeded usage billed as burst credits).
- Latency target: we can commit to p95 < 250ms and p99 < 700ms for the 13B path under normal operating conditions. We’ll include detailed SLO language in the MAP.

Pricing anchor (ballpark):
- 6 reserved A100-eq GPUs: $120k / month list (before discount)
- Burst pool (4 GPUs) sizing & credits: add-on, nominally $25k / month list if continuously available; usually provided as burst credits with limited daily minutes.
- 70B reserved pool (2 GPUs): $45k / month list
- Suggested commercial posture: 12-month commit with 18% list discount + 2 months onboarding credit. We’ll include an alternate 24-month price with ~24% discount.

I’ve looped Marissa and Ben to confirm the technical assumptions and to draft the MAP. We’ll send the draft pricing table + MAP and required SOC2 link by tomorrow EOD.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: alternate sizing notes for ApexMed

Karthik / Ben —

A few notes from sizing review (keeping procurement asks in mind):

1) Microbatching & request shaping: if ApexMed is willing to accept a mild increase in p95 (~+30–50ms) we can collapse more requests into larger microbatches and reduce reserved GPU count by ~25%. That would move the 13B reserved from 6 -> 4 GPUs while still meeting p99 target most of the time.

2) KV caching: with aggressive prefix caching (their chats often re-use system prompts & patient history) we can shave token compute for a large % of requests — estimate effective tokens/request down to ~150 tokens for cached flows.

3) Hybrid commit: propose 4x reserved GPUs + autoscale to 8x for spikes, with burst credits covering 120 minutes/month of elevated usage. Commercially we can price this as a lower commit + a burst allowance. It’s an attractive middle ground for procurement.

4) 70B traffic: recommend keeping that work on pay-as-you-go or a small 2 GPU reserved pool only if they want guaranteed latency for those calls.

I’ll prepare a short pros/cons table and a revised pricing line for 4-reserved vs 6-reserved and the burst credit option.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: alternate sizing notes for ApexMed

Agree with Marissa. Quick commercial framing we should offer to ApexMed: 

Option A (Conservative) — 6 reserved GPUs + 4 burst GPUs
- Guarantees the 350 r/s SLA with low variance.
- 12-month: 18% discount + 2 months onboarding credit.

Option B (Rightsized hybrid) — 4 reserved GPUs + autoscale to 8 (burst credits)
- Lower committed spend (roughly 25% lower monthly committed cost vs Option A).
- 12-month: 15% discount + 3 months onboarding credit.

Option C (Pay-as-you-go plus small reserve for critical flows) — 2 reserved GPUs + PAYG for the rest
- Lowest up-front cost but no throughput guarantee; useful if they want to validate.

I’d push them toward B as a procurement compromise — lower commit, still guarantees via burst policy (documented in MAP). If procurement presses on price we can offer an additional one-time onboarding credit in lieu of deeper discount.

—Ben
Director, Sales Engineering

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@apexmed.com>, procurement@apexmed.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: ApexMed proposal: hybrid commit with burst credits (MAP + pricing attached)

Sarah —

Thanks for the profile and patience. Attached is a short MAP and two commercial options so your procurement team can pick the posture that fits budget vs. guarantee. Attached: redwood_map_v1.docx and pricing_table_q4v2.xlsx.

High-level options: 
- Option A (Guarantee-forward): 6 reserved A100-eq GPUs for 13B traffic + 2 reserved for 70B, burst pool of 4 GPUs for spikes. 12-month term, 18% discount, 2 months onboarding credit. Covers sustained 350 r/s with headroom.

- Option B (Rightsize / Hybrid): 4 reserved A100-eq GPUs + autoscale to 8 via burst credits (we provide 120 minutes/month of guaranteed burst), 70B on PAYG or small 2 GPU reserved pool. 12-month term, 15% discount + 3 months onboarding credit. Lower committed spend; slightly higher p95 in worst-case microbatching scenario.

Other items: 
- SOC2 link: https://redwoodinference.com/trust/soc2 (procurement can use this link directly)
- SLA language: throughput-backed clause for Option A; for Option B we document burst minutes and fallback behavior in the MAP.

Next step: let us know which option procurement prefers. If you want to push pricing, we can consider an incremental commercial concession in exchange for 24-month term or a defined usage minimum.

Attachments: redwood_map_v1.docx, pricing_table_q4v2.xlsx

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ApexMed proposal: hybrid commit with burst credits (MAP + pricing attached)

Karthik —

Appreciate the thorough options. A couple follow-ups from procurement & infra: 

1) Can you commit to p99 < 700ms for the 13B path in Option B as well, or is that only in Option A? If it’s only in A we’ll need to know typical p99 ranges for B under peak as well.
2) If we sign a 12-month roadmap with Option B, can you bump the discount to 18% (you offered 15%) and provide 60 minutes additional burst credit for the first 3 months?
3) On SOC2 we’ll pull the link; procurement also wants a short summary of data retention and log access for audits (one pager).

We’re prepared to move quickly if we can reach a small commercial middle ground on discount + initial burst minutes.

—Sarah
Head of Platform, ApexMed

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@apexmed.com>, procurement@apexmed.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ApexMed proposal: hybrid commit with burst credits (MAP + pricing attached)

Sarah / Procurement —

Quick internal alignment and response:

- Option B p99 behavior: with the 4-reserved + autoscale to 8 configuration and the burst credits we typically see p99 in the ~550–750ms band under spike conditions depending on model mix and how many concurrent 70B calls are routed into the same pool. We can commit to a p99 < 750ms SLA for Option B with documented exceptions for 70B traffic and extreme multi-region failures. If you require p99 < 700ms as a hard commitment, that remains in Option A.

- Commercial counter: we can move Option B to 18% discount (matching Option A) for a 12-month term if ApexMed accepts a capped surge billing model (burst credits + any additional burst beyond allowance billed at published burst rates). We will also provide +60 minutes/month of extra burst for the first 3 months as onboarding support.

- Deliverables: we’ll include a one-page data retention & audit summary in the final MAP package and attach SOC2 evidence link.

If that sounds good I’ll have contracts & final MAP updated for signature and ask legal to prepare the SOW.

Thanks — appreciate the quick collaboration.

Karthik
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
